## Executive briefing
- One lead investment story qualified this week (YELLOW). No RED/ORANGE stories met our bar.
- U.S. nursing shortage remains structurally tight; AMN’s Nov 5 print showed travel-nurse revenue +19% YoY and CMS launched a $275M nursing‑home staffing campaign in late October, reinforcing demand for temporary nurses and nursing education programs. ([ir.amnhealthcare.com](https://ir.amnhealthcare.com/2026-11-05-AMN-HEALTHCARE-ANNOUNCES-THIRD-QUARTER-2026-RESULTS?asPDF=1&utm_source=openai))
- BDC look‑through to private travel‑nurse provider Medical Solutions is real but small; importantly, PSBD’s exposure was on non‑accrual as of Sep 30, 2026, limiting current income transmission. ([palmersquarebdc.com](https://www.palmersquarebdc.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-446165/psbd-20260930.htm?utm_source=openai))
- A short‑lived fresh‑strawberry tightness followed California rain (late Oct/early Nov); public‑equity leverage is weak and transitory—kept in Monitoring below. ([markon.com](https://www.markon.com/update-california-strawberries-84/?utm_source=openai))
- No continuing stories from prior weeks had a material update inside the Nov 5–Nov 12 window.

## Monitoring signals
- Strawberry shortage (late‑Oct to early‑Nov disruption)
  - What we have: Markon field reports and USDA/AMS Nov 4 weekly indicate rain‑related losses and a seasonal wind‑down in California with early Mexico volumes still building. ([markon.com](https://www.markon.com/update-california-strawberries-84/?utm_source=openai))
  - What would move it upward: Evidence that tightness persists into December with visible margin commentary from a listed operator (e.g., DOLE) or a materially adverse update for key California tenants/leases (LAND), or a final AD ruling in Jan 2027 that resets winter price structures. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1857475/000185747526000094/dole-20260930.htm?utm_source=openai))

## Rejected or low-value signals
- “Mexican farmers’ strike” affecting strawberries — rejected: unsupported viral claim for this commodity; no authoritative corroboration specific to strawberries. (unsupported viral claim)
- Private‑only exposure tables for berry marketers (e.g., Driscoll’s, Naturipe partners) — rejected: private‑company‑only exposure with negligible listed look‑through. (private-company-only exposure)

## Analyst-quality flags
- PSBD income transmission overstated: Analyst said BDC loans to Medical Solutions generate floating‑rate interest income; PSBD’s Medical Solutions position was on non‑accrual as of Sep 30, 2026, limiting current income until it returns to accrual—material for instrument‑specific mapping. We corrected the mechanism and modestly reduced confidence in BDC income sensitivity. ([palmersquarebdc.com](https://www.palmersquarebdc.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-446165/psbd-20260930.htm?utm_source=openai))
- CMS policy sourcing strengthened: Replaced secondary press coverage with CMS primary pages (campaign page, MLN newsletter, and FAQs specifying the Oct 26, 2026 start of the 90‑day exception window) to support the $275M initiative. ([cms.gov](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/health-safety-standards/quality-safety-oversight-general-information/cms-nursing-home-staffing-campaign?utm_source=openai))
- Ownership/name verification: Confirmed Adtalem’s Feb 5, 2026 rename to Covista via SEC exhibits; no inconsistencies found with ticker transition to CVSA. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/730464/000110465926011611/atge-20260205xex3d2.htm?utm_source=openai))

## Next-week watchlist
- U.S. nursing shortage
  - Move-up: AMN or peers signal stronger‑than‑seasonal travel‑nurse demand into Q4/Q1 or CMS publishes early uptake metrics for the staffing campaign.
  - Move-down: Clear multi‑week deterioration in travel volumes/rates or hospital operator disclosures showing sharp contract‑labor normalization.
  - Drop: If multiple quarters show sustained agency demand declines and education‑pipeline growth stalls without offsetting policy support.
- Strawberry shortage
  - Move-up: Persistent tightness beyond late November with DOLE commentary on berries margin impact, or AD final determination pointing to meaningfully higher winter import costs.
  - Move-down: Rapid Mexico/Florida ramp with USDA prices normalizing within 2–4 weeks.
  - Drop: Clear normalization in USDA AMS movement/prices and retailer availability.
